newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks fade at open after Dow and metals fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks fade at open after Dow and metals fall.

text.p: Australian shares drifted lower from the open on Tuesday as investors followed negative leads from Wall Street and commodity markets, where base metal prices crumbled.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 13.3 points down at 2,323.0.
Another significant negative factor for the market early was National Australia Bank stock which went ex-dividend, paying a final dividend of 44 cents (US$0.35) per share.
"It's no surprise where the market has opened and I expect it to trade in a range between 10 to 20 points down on the day," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said volume was thin as the market wound down towards the Christmas break.
Stocks opened down across the board with the bank sector suffering the worst decline due to the change in the basis of quotation for National Australia Bank stock.
The retail sector, although slightly lower, was fairing better than other industrials and dealers said investors were looking for a stronger Christmas trading period this year.
